I will read packet.json and review the final plan-only correction and strategy for azguard P4.Beginning a read-only review of the azguard P4 final plan correction and strategy.

Confirmed the review scope is strictly read-only. I will check for contract, order, and strategy errors against the three core requirements: accepted D15 order, restored P4 prefix dependencies and phase/batch order, and preserved statuses, results, contracts, and memberships.

The review now targets specific contract and order rules. Prefix dependencies must not hide unfinished earlier producers. Batch start logic must treat earlier requested members as satisfying while keeping B4a and B4e valid. P4.9 is blocked and cannot achieve product or acceptance GREEN. The previous minor in_progress observation is resolved by a finish blocked state. The strategy correctly schedules P4.6 review-route recovery before bounded predecessor runs. Scoping checks and final review remain strictly within authorized scope.

B4a and B4e memberships remain intact after reordering. All batches mode is preserved as "recommended". Prefix dependencies are being verified against the D15 sequence; P4.1 through P4.7 show correct prefix dependencies.

Prefix dependencies verified through P4.11. P4.9 depends on the full prefix, and P4.10 depends on P4.9 within B4e. The batch start nuance is being checked.

The batch start nuance is confirmed correct. B4a and B4e dependencies are valid because earlier members satisfy within the same batch. All statuses match before and after states.

P4.7 and P4.8 are completed out of order, depending on blocked P4.6 and todo P4.19. P4.9 is confirmed blocked in both before and after states; the prior review incorrectly recorded it as in_progress.

The prior in_progress finding for P4.9 is resolved because the packet now shows blocked in both before and after states. Statuses, results, contracts, and memberships are preserved. All dependencies match the D15 prefix.

The packet omits actual contract and result text, so preservation of those fields is only asserted by proof flags. Statuses are verifiable from the items array.

No demonstrated error exists for missing contract or result payloads. The packet lacks before and after diffs for those fields, so inventing a finding would be speculative. P4.9 dependencies are already confirmed equal in both states.

P4.9's before_dependencies were already complete, so the correction only restored empty prefix dependencies for the remaining items. The next field shows kind "waiting", exact "waiting: blocked P4.6", phase "P4", batch "BP4-19", and an empty items list.

A potential order error is emerging. The blocked item P4.6 belongs to batch BP4-6, yet the next object assigns it batch BP4-19. This mismatch between the blocked item's actual batch and the next field's batch value is under review.

The batch mismatch is now viewed as a contract error. The next field should report the blocked item's own batch, BP4-6, rather than the next downstream batch, BP4-19.

Reconsidering the batch mismatch. The scheduler frontier is P4.6, the earliest undone item in D15 order. The next field may indicate the batch of the next runnable item rather than the blocked item's own batch.

The refusal checks confirm P4.10, P4.11, and P4.20 all wait for the blocked P4.6 specifically, not for todo items in between. This supports the conclusion that next.batch should be BP4-6 rather than BP4-19.

The prefix dependency rule is confirmed correct. P4.7 is done but still waits for blocked P4.6, because the prefix intentionally prevents an already-completed out-of-order item from masking unfinished earlier producers.

P4.8 is confirmed done_with_deviations and later items still wait for it, which is correct.

The next.batch discrepancy is being reconsidered. The field may indicate the next batch the scheduler would attempt to schedule rather than the blocked item's own batch. Since P4.6 is blocked, the scheduler has moved to BP4-19 but reports waiting because of P4.6. The items array is empty and route, launch, and command are null.

The strategy text matches next.exact and next.reason, but never mentions batch BP4-19. Without the planner source or command access, the contract semantics for next.batch cannot be verified. Speculating that BP4-19 is wrong would be hypothetical. Only a demonstrated error can be reported.

The strategy's post-P4.6 sequence is being checked against the D15 order. The packet lists P4.19, P4.16, P4.18, P4.15, P4.13, P4.20, P4.21, and P4.9 after P4.6. The D15 sequence between those items includes P4.7 and P4.8. The review is verifying whether the strategy correctly skips already-closed items.

The strategy correctly skips already-closed P4.7 and P4.8. The remaining sequence matches D15 order exactly.

The strategy correctly requires reopening P4.9 from blocked to todo after its dependencies achieve GREEN status, using the owner's decision as the reopen basis. The refusal check confirms this exact path. The review is now questioning whether reopening P4.9 after GREEN dependencies is the correct sequencing.

The review confirms reopening P4.9 after its dependencies achieve GREEN is correct. A blocked item cannot start until its dependencies are ready. The strategy's final check is a plan schema and cycle validation, not product acceptance. The prior review correctly distinguished plan checks from product results.

The economy section aligns with the no-unrelated-packages rule. It restricts checks to the owning package and its dependency closure, and explicitly excludes Swissknifeman, Vaulter, Filament, and fleet health.

The next.reason field contains P4.6's native blocked stderr text, confirming the scheduler is correctly identifying the P4.6 blocker. The batch field showing BP4-19 is now viewed as a likely payload bug rather than a contract error.

Walking the batch list confirms BP4-6 is the first unsatisfied batch, so next.batch should be BP4-6. Reporting BP4-19 is a demonstrated error in the correction's reported next state.

The scheduler may be skipping blocked batches when computing the next runnable batch. This would explain why next.batch shows BP4-19 instead of BP4-6. The operator is not instructed to start BP4-19 because kind is waiting and items is empty. The exact reason string correctly identifies P4.6 as the blocker.

The batch mismatch is being reconsidered as a potential payload bug rather than a contract error. The user's explicit instruction that intra-batch prefix dependencies are valid prevents flagging those cases. All prefix dependencies now match the D15 order.

The reopen API is the only available path to move P4.9 from blocked to todo, so following the tool's own error message is correct and not a defect. The packet contains no explicit after_phase_order array. The items list is in D15 order, which satisfies the strategy's claim that phase.items aligns with D15. This is not a demonstrated contract error.
